blocks.h2: Hot Water Demands in Evanston Restaurants
blocks.body: A restaurant kitchen uses hot water constantly: handwashing, prep sinks, dish machines and cleanup. Health codes set temperatures for some of these, and a heater that can't keep up shows up fast during a busy service. We size commercial heaters around peak demand, not average use, and keep them running with scheduled flushing and descaling. When grease is part of the problem downstream, we clear and jet those lines too.

Evanston's businesses range from busy restaurants downtown to salons on Central Street and shops along Main Street and Chicago Avenue. Many work out of older buildings where the water heater was added long after the building went up. We trace the piping, check the venting and keep a record of each unit, so repairs are faster and replacements can be planned.

blocks.h2: What Affects the Price of Commercial Water Heater Work
blocks.body: Capacity, fuel and venting drive most of the price. Older downtown buildings can add steps, like tracing unusual piping or upgrading venting to meet current code. Getting equipment in and out of a basement or back room matters too. We look at all of it and quote one flat price before work starts.
